sources: For one resolved provider route, provider execution shall perform no more than the configured retry maximum-attempt count before surfacing the final failure to routing.
Sync and async exhausted retry each perform exactly the configured maximum attempt count and never one interaction beyond.
answer.test_focus: After async retries run out on a temporary provider error, the test must check that the exception raised is the original provider exception (same type and instance), not a tenacity RetryError, and that exactly max_attempts calls were made.

answer.reason: TREQ_PROVIDER_RETRY_BOUNDS says the final failure must reach routing once retries run out. With reraise=False, Tenacity wraps that failure in a tenacity.RetryError instead of re-raising the provider's own exception. The attempt count stays the same, but routing gets a different exception type than the one the provider raised, so it may no longer tell a temporary failure from a permanent one.
answer.test_focus: Make every attempt fail with a retryable provider error until the retries run out. Check that the caller gets that same provider exception (same type and instance), not tenacity.RetryError, and that exactly max_attempts calls were made.
